checks.claim: C1: The target uses the original full H:homog class, data (1,0), the actual source field, and a physical mask applied after smoothing. Pointwise covariance nonnegativity comes from a nonnegative Radon Gamma.
checks.reason: Target lines 6-9 match canonical H:homog (excerpt lines 135-154): d=1,2,3; a in (0,1); 0<alpha<d or alpha=d=1; alpha+a<2; nonnegative even positive-definite tempered Radon Gamma. Target line 14 is notes (5) at equal widths. K_delta>0 because it is a Laplace integral, and Gamma_(2epsilon)=p_(2epsilon)*Gamma>=0 because a positive heat kernel is integrated against a nonnegative measure, so PSD alone is not the source of the sign (crosswalk lines 39-40). Notes Sections 5-6 supply the jointly continuous, spatially smooth version per fixed rho, without using a density, so singular and invariant-direction Gamma are covered. The coefficient m(x)Y_rho sits after smoothing, and no multiplier on the raw noise quotient is presumed.

checks.claim: C2: F1 holds for all n,k, including unequal and empty chains, self-pairings, and arbitrary terminal x,y, with finite integrals and unsmoothed d3 sphere measures.
checks.reason: Independently verified. At fixed rho, |C_rho|<=K_delta(0)Gamma_(2epsilon)(0) by Cauchy-Schwarz, and the iterated Green measures are positive with total masses controlled by (2.4). Gaussian moments are uniformly bounded, so Fubini applies to the pathwise iterated integrals of the continuous version. Isserlis then gives zero at odd total order and, at even order, the finite sum over all pair partitions of the n+k vertices, self-pairings included. Each diagram integrand is a positive Green measure times a nonnegative C_rho product times prod m(x_v), and that mask product depends only on the vertices, not the pairing. Since 0<=prod m<=1, both inequalities hold diagram by diagram. In d3 the integrals are successive sphere integrals of continuous functions, so no density is needed. The t=0 and empty-chain cases are trivial.

checks.claim: C3: F2 gives absolute L2 convergence with the same q_n, and the sums identify with ordinary mild solutions without global supremum moments or sample positivity.
checks.reason: F1 at x=y,k=n gives ||X^m_(rho,n)(t,x)||_2<=||X_(rho,n)(t,x)||_2<=q_n(t), uniformly in rho and x, by L:vertex-crude with q_0>=1. Summability of q_n follows from E:vertex-summability. For identification, let B be the supremum of |Y_rho| on a compact backward cone. Green mass t-s and induction give the pathwise majorant |X_n|<=B^n t^(2n)/(2n)!, so the series converges uniformly on the cone to a continuous mild solution, and Gronwall on cones gives uniqueness among locally bounded solutions. An L2-convergent subsequence of partial sums identifies the L2 sum with the pathwise sum on the fixed-rho full-measure set. Only cone-local boundedness is used. No sample positivity is claimed (target lines 62-63 and 91).

checks.claim: C4: F2a and F2b are correct, using nonnegative diagrams, L2 products, Bochner positive averaging, and only unmasked stationarity plus Cauchy-Schwarz.
checks.reason: Finite partial-sum products converge in L1 by L2 convergence, and the double series is dominated by q_n q_k, so F1 sums to F2a in any order. Each diagram is continuous in x,y, by the sphere or ball parametrization and bounded continuous integrands, so the two-point function is continuous and x->u(t,x) is L2 continuous. With the uniform L2 bound and phi in L1, this gives the Bochner integral, which agrees with the pathwise integral by Fubini. Inner-product continuity then gives the double integral of phi(x)phi(y)E[u^m u^m], which F2a bounds by the unmasked double integral because phi>=0. Unmasked stationarity follows from the translation-invariant covariance and data, and Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||phi||_1^2 E|u_rho(t,0)|^2. No point Sobolev evaluation or signed or velocity ordering is used. The target asserts Bochner existence without displaying this route, but the route closes.

checks.claim: C5: F3 follows, with the unmasked limit derived from canonical inputs and the masked L2 limit kept as an explicit assumption.
checks.reason: At common widths the source law matches the canonical edge covariances (excerpt lines 1053-1054 and 1065-1067; notes (5)). L:joint-fixed-order gives every diagram limit at arbitrary relative rates, including unequal and empty chains, with Green-before-noise in d3. E:mixed-moment and E:full-second identify the limiting sum, whose construction is noncircular per excerpt lines 484-497. Dominated convergence with q_n q_k gives lim E|u_rho(t,0)|^2=E|u(t,0)|^2 using only single-rho laws, so no pathwise identification is needed. If the averages converge in L2 to A_m, their second moments converge, and F2b gives F3 along the net or the specified sequence. Lines 73-86 keep existence, Young identification, local phase, and rates as non-conclusions. Note: crosswalk line 37 calls this an accepted moment limit, while the accepted notes (lines 8-10 and 471-472) list the transfer as open. It is a correct new derivation from accepted ingredients and must be written out in the proof.

checks.claim: C6: The finite check algorithm and its negative controls match their description and scope.
checks.reason: Line audit: Gamma=delta_x1 tensor Leb_x2 is admissible with alpha=1 and a=.5. heat_zero=1/sqrt(4 pi epsilon) equals Gamma_(2epsilon)(0). kappa matches K_delta at v=0 and v!=0 via the lower incomplete gamma function. The G2 constant and cone condition are correct, with minimum dt .2 exceeding maximum |dx| .1. Coincident Gaussians at x1=0 are legitimate because the covariance has no x2 dependence, so the variance of their difference is 0. Chains have the n Green factors of (2.15), are oriented earliest to terminal, end in data 1, and carry the mask on vertices only. The Isserlis recursion includes self-pairings. The JSON has 4x25=100 rows, 48 of them odd and zero; the row symmetries hold, and masked<=full in every row. All even rows other than (0,0) have ratio below 1. I reproduced by hand: (x=y=.05,n=k=1) full about .0079244 versus JSON .0079245, with ratio exactly .5625=((1+.5)/2)^2; and (x=y=.05,n=0,k=2) full about .0048976 versus JSON .0048976. The PSD difference c[[0,1/2],[1/2,3/4]] has eigenvalues -c/4 and c. The signed observable has raw variance 0 and masked variance c/4. Neither is claimed as a velocity counterexample, and no continuum certification is claimed. Note: the strict-decrease claim is evidenced by the JSON rows, not asserted per row by the script, and the negative controls use analytic literals.

checks.reason: No counterexample, wrong constant, missing hypothesis, or failed implication was found. Every step is either elementary positivity or Gaussian calculus at fixed rho, or a named accepted input. This is a statement-level audit, not a proof certificate.
